title: How Identity Labeling Drives Content Engagement and Sales
summary: Amelia Willingham Gonzamonte analyzes a viral video to explain how identity labeling drives video engagement and sales. By accurately describing an audience's traits or problems and assigning a distinct label to them, creators make viewers feel understood. This sense of validation builds trust and makes the audience feel that a product or service was built specifically for them.
key_points: Identity labeling drives high video performance because people naturally seek categories (like Enneagram, love languages, or astrology) that explain who they are and how to handle their issues.
When a creator articulates a problem better than the audience can express it, it creates an immediate 'that is so me' reaction within seconds.
When viewers feel seen, they place higher trust in the creator and perceive the product or service as specifically tailored for them.
To apply identity labeling in content, call out specific characteristics, problems, or tendencies of your target clientele.
Associate those target characteristics with a specific label connected to your product, service, or methodology.
Effective labels are typically relieving, flattering, illuminating, validating, or aspirational.
Skincare example line: 'You don't have to be a skincare addict to have perfect skin. You just need the XYZ routine.'
Interior design example line: 'You're not a lazy decorator, you're a minimalist – and you can still make your home look intentional.'
Sales coaching example line: '	'I'm too introverted for sales' – if this is you, you're a X sales type who hasn't learned Y methodology yet.'
content: Post text: This video went viral because of a SUPER simple marketing rule. Here's how you can use it for your content: Call out specific characteristics of your clientele (MUST BE SPECIFIC). It could be about problems they're facing, tendencies they have, habits they repeat… etc. Then associate those characteristics with a SPECIFIC LABEL that has to do with one of your products, services, or solutions. And it works best when the label is either: Relieving, flattering, illuminating, validating, or aspirational. Because people share and save content that makes them say: “Wait… this is me.” Here are a few examples of this in action: Skincare: “You don’t have to be a skincare addict to have perfect skin. You just need the ‘XYZ’ routine.” Nutrition: “If you have constant gut issues with no allergies or explanation, you likely have X, and here’s how you’re gonna solve it.” Financial Planner: “if you just want to invest a little cash a month without having to think about where to put it, you’re an ‘X’ investor who needs the ‘XYZ’ strategy” Interior Designer: “You’re not a lazy decorator, you’re a minimalist – and you can still make your home look intentional” Productivity Coach: “if you find yourself struggling with deadlines but your mind is always going – you’re an X thinker, and you need the XYZ planning system.” Personal Stylist: “If you feel like you ‘can’t wear dresses’ – you’re an X body type that needs the XYZ silhouette.” Sales Coach: “‘I’m too introverted for sales’ – if this is you, you’re a X sales type who hasn’t learned Y methodology yet.” This is one of the coolest ways to show off the unique offers or methodologies you have that set you apart from competitors. Try it out, and happy creating!✨ Creator featured: @coachvalj. Spoken transcript: Speaker 1: This video proves that identity sells. Speaker 2: You're not going to like this. But if you can explain your problem better than you can demonstrate your progress, you got that SS. That's that sophisticated stagnation. Speaker 1: Why did this video get over 2.8 million views? Three seconds into this video, like 50% of us are going to be saying, that is so me, and we're going to watch to the end to see what she has to say about us. Now, why is that? It's because of something called identity labeling. It's why we love Enneagram, love languages, and astrology. We love to be given an identity that tells us who we are and how we can solve our specific problems. So by leading with this kind of identity labeling, she makes her audience feel seen. And when people feel seen, they don't just trust you more, they start to see your product or service as made for them. Therefore, they're way more likely to buy. How can you use it in your content? See the caption.
